newsitem.title: INDIA: Crisil lowers Jindal Steel bond rating.
newsitem.headline: Crisil lowers Jindal Steel bond rating.

text.p: The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (Crisil) said on Tuesday it downgraded rating on Jindal Vijayanagar Steel Ltd's 6.35 billion rupee non-convertible bond issue to "BBB-" from "BBB."
"The revised rating indicates that the degree of safety regarding timely payment of interest and principal is moderate," Crisil said in a statement.
"The downgrading reflects principally the increased risk in project funding," Crisil said.

The project cost for the 1.6 million tonnes a year hot-rolled steel project using Corex technology has risen to 41.38 billion rupees due to change of scope of the project and the rupee's depreciation from the earlier estimate of 33.0 billion rupees, the rating agency said.

The increase in cost is to be partly funded through debt and partly through additional equity contribution of 1.26 billion rupees from the promoters which has to be brought in by March 1998, Crisil said.
"The gearing on the project has thus increased from the originally envisaged 1.81 to 2.18."
Jindal has partly-paid up shares on which 4.7 billion rupees is expected to be collected including 2.11 billion rupees from Jindal group companies and their associates, Crisil said.
"The Jindal group companies are expected to face a liquidity crunch due to ongoing projects in the Jindal group as well as financial commitments in other group companies," it said.
"Additionally, 2.5 billion rupees has to be collected from the public/financial institutions/mutual funds etc as call money from the equity issue," it said.
Since the fully paid up shares of the company are presently quoting below par value, the uncertainty of getting the funds from the public has increased, Crisil said.
The HR steel project has also been delayed by six months, it added.
